name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Adopt the 4px focus ring at 7:1 contrast. It meets WCAG AAA for low vision, ensuring keyboard users see focus clearly without overwhelming the interface. The trade-off is slightly more visual weight, but it’s necessary for users who rely on focus indicators to navigate.

name: Reader
text: The 4px ring at 7:1 contrast fails AAA for users with tunnel vision or cognitive load—they need a *thicker* ring (6px) to *locate* focus, not just see it. A 6px ring at 4.5:1 meets AA for low vision *and* AAA for contrast, while still being usable on high-DPI screens. Test both with real users who have tunnel vision to settle it.

name: Ramp
text:
Adopt the 6px focus ring at 4.5:1 contrast. It meets WCAG AA for low vision and AAA for contrast, ensuring keyboard users can *locate* focus without cognitive strain. The trade-off is a bolder ring that may feel heavier in dense interfaces, but it’s the only way to balance visibility, usability, and compliance for all users.
[dispatched 2 workers: worker-3204, worker-3227 — done, dissolved]

name: Reader
text: The 6px ring at 4.5:1 risks failing users with high-DPI screens where the ring blurs into a 5px or 3px band, making it harder to spot than a crisp 4px ring at 7:1. Test both rings on a 4K screen at 200% zoom with real keyboard users—if the 6px ring doesn’t collapse into a fuzzy line, it’s the safer choice.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Finalize 4px focus ring at 7:1 contrast with 1px outer glow (white) — deliver as CSS variable in EXCAVA’s design system, owned by Ramp.
